To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the specific resistance of ohmic contacts of CdTe depends on the bulk resisti vity of the CdTe and on the oxygen concentration of the CdTe, that the specific resistance increases as a function of the contact time, and that the specific resistance can be reduced by the use of phosphorus as a dopant.

the ‘specific’ contact resistances of ohmically contacted p-type CdTe crystals depend linearly on their bulk resistivity, and that the contact resistances increase with time for most of the investigated metals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of ohmic contacts with a low contact resistance to p-type Cd Te.
the development of low-resistance ohmic contacts to CdS and CdTe.
the following topics: (1) Ohmic contacts to n-type CdS, (2) ohmic contacts to n- and p-type CdTe, and (3) ohmic contacts between n- and p- type CdS/CdS heterojunction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the contact resistances are not stable.
the contacts are ohmic but that the contact resistivity is time dependent.
the contact properties of p-type CdTe cannot be predicted with certainty.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ohmic contacts can be made with a specific contact resistance r = 0.07 Ω cm.
the ohmic contact properties of the CdTe samples are determined by the phosphorus concentration and the oxygen content.
the contact resistivity of the investigated contacts to phosphorous-doped p-type CdTe is not as low as desired, and that the contact resistances are not stable enough for practical applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ohmic contacts to CdS/Cd Te solar cells should be stable for at least 1 year, and that they should be stable under illumination.
the ohmic contact quality to CdTe is not only dependent on the doping level, but also on the oxygen content of this material.
ohmic contacts to CdS/ CdTe solar cell structures are not stable over the long term.
